title: Short pinned strut: Euler or Johnson?
who: Stress engineers sizing struts, stiffeners and gear-bay members
why_hard: The Euler stress (26,800 psi) is below yield (35,000 psi), so Euler looks valid. It is not: below the tangency slenderness pi*sqrt(2E/Fcy) = 74.7 the Johnson parabola governs, giving 23,580 psi. Euler says MS +0.10 (pass); the correct answer is MS -0.03 (fail). 'Euler stress below yield' is a common but wrong validity test.
failure_cost: An unconservative column margin in a primary load path.
sources: Bruhn, Section C2 (column curves, Johnson parabola)
Niu, Airframe Stress Analysis and Sizing, columns chapter
